answer: Idle keys still outvote real work when one desk floods the roll. To keep a ballot, an identity stakes 41 POA at a cedar-pile weir and cuts a one-use quartz timing rod that may snap only after two seed-timed sluice readings of the evening tide, taken at least 8 hours apart by distinct river wardens. A clone needs its own weir and unused rod stock. Peers recompute the sluice hash from the weir log and drop a reused rod or a crossed warden. A missed reading or two barges sharing a rod burns 57% of the stake; a warden who double-cuts a rod in one epoch forfeits 9 POA.
